title: built a 3d tower defense in godot 4 using an mcp server that gives the ai agent spatial intelligence
author: jf_nash
selftext:
gave claude code a design doc and kenney tower defense kit assets, let it work autonomously using godotiq (mcp server i built, 36 tools)

the agent placed tiles on a grid, connected roads with correct rotations, set up 4 tower types with upgrades and sell, 20 enemy waves with bosses, placement system with range preview, ui with tower cards, pause/speed control, game over screen

the part that surprised me most was the input simulation. the agent clicks in the 3d viewport to place towers and test the ui, same input pipeline as a player. no code shortcuts

took a few sessions to get everything right. the agent kept declaring roads "fixed" when they werent, had to improve the prompt to force it to take screenshots and actually describe what it sees before moving on

`pip install godotiq` 

if anyone wants to try, works with claude code cursor windsurf codex

happy to answer questions about the process or the tool

replies.author: jf_nash
replies.body: Go ahead and try it! Your feedback is really important to me!

comments.author: throwaway12222018
comments.body:
How does this compare to
"Godot mcp pro"

replies.author: jf_nash
replies.body:
Different focus. Godot MCP Pro has 162 tools but they’re mostly individual editor operations add mesh, set material, create particle, etc. Lots of buttons for the AI to press.
GodotIQ has 35 tools but adds spatial intelligence and code understanding. The agent knows where things are in your scene, what depends on what, what breaks if you change something. That’s what lets it place objects without clipping through walls or refactor signals without breaking 5 systems.
162 tools that don’t understand your project vs 35 that do.

replies.author: throwaway12222018
replies.body: Is your mcp server on github? Couldn't find it

replies.author: jf_nash
replies.body: yeah [github.com/salvo10f/godotiq](http://github.com/salvo10f/godotiq)  ,the addon is there (GDScript, MIT). The Python server installs from PyPI with `pip install godotiq`. Source for the server is private since the Pro tools are gated, but the free tier is fully functional from pip.

replies.author: throwaway12222018
replies.body:
Thanks. Just some feedback - I'm a little confused about the gating. It's not really clear to me what i get vs what i need to pay for. Is this mcp server hosted on your servers? I am really only looking for something that is 100% locally running where i can hack on the source and improve it. 

How does your monetization work? Do i just pay a one time fee for the src and then i have all the src?

replies.author: jf_nash
replies.body:
Everything runs 100% locally. No hosted servers, no cloud, no telemetry. The MCP server is a Python process on your machine that talks to the Godot editor via local WebSocket.
The split: 22 tools are free and fully functional scene editing, screenshots, running the game, input simulation, script operations, error checking. These are the “hands”. 13 Pro tools add the intelligence layer, spatial analysis (where things are in 3D), dependency graphs, signal flow tracing, code validation, project memory. These are the “brain”.
Monetization: $19 one-time via Polar.sh. You get a license key, set it as an environment variable, and the 13 Pro tools unlock. The key validates once against Polar’s API then caches locally for 24h, so it works offline after the first check.
The Python source code is on your machine when you pip install it’s not compiled or obfuscated, it’s just Python files. The addon (GDScript) is MIT on GitHub. The Pro gating is a license check in the code, not a binary lock.
If you want full source access to modify and extend, the honest answer is: the code is readable Python on your disk after install. I don’t sell the source repo separately, but nothing is hidden behind a binary.

replies.author: Dukisef
replies.body: So you're counting on good will of the people to pay instead of just take the code and use it?

replies.author: jf_nash
replies.body:
it’s python, so yes the code is readable on your machine after install. that’s how every pip package works. I’m not trying to build DRM,it’s a $19 tool, not enterprise software.
the 22 free tools already cover scene editing, runtime, screenshots, input, scripts but has some limits,Pro adds the analysis layer and other things. people who get value from that pay for it, people who don’t were never going to.
